title: W07c: pre-implementation Hermes identity and dispatch feasibility gates
description: Verify the host capabilities needed by W07a/W07b before those implementations begin. Recheck the selected native Hermes executable/build stamp and test host-provided durable session/lineage identity for normal and delegated workers, parallel sessions in one profile, reconnect/resume identity, runtime/profile-scoped native MCP dispatch to an explicit project server, required allowlists/grants, and adapter-supplied request context reaching the temporary Waystation server. Use a minimal temporary probe harness over the W06 contracts and W08b host bridge; this is capability evidence, not a second binding store or full worker adapter. A missing or ambiguous capability blocks worker implementation pending an explicit design decision; do not substitute model text, startup cwd, UI selection, one profile per worker or a Hermes core fork. Record actual commands, selected build, results and remaining host limits. W07a/W07b own production bindings/forwarding, W08d owns package assembly, and W09 owns installed end-to-end acceptance. Implementation baseline: merged main 6276d5f / ledger closure e64d4bd, Waystation 0.6.0 on Bun 1.4.1; see docs/reconciliation-2026-09-27.md. Reuse the merged foundation and its tests.
acceptance: Plan 12.5 host-capability prerequisites have reproducible pass/fail evidence against the selected Hermes build, including normal/delegated identity, parallel profile sessions, resume identity and native MCP project routing.
Disabled plugins, absent allowlists/grants and unavailable or ambiguous host context refuse explicitly; failure blocks W07a/W07b rather than selecting another architecture.
The probe uses isolated temporary ledgers and Hermes configuration, never mutates live project tasks or live plugin settings, and cleans up only its own fixture resources.
The probe requires neither production worker bindings nor the final assembled plugin; installed cross-component behavior remains W09 acceptance and no circular package dependency is introduced.
notes:
Gate failure is recorded for a separate design decision rather than silently choosing another architecture.

POC-first decision (2026-09-27): deferred behind task-poc-value-review. Keep this full-plan task todo. A completed review, including a negative/stop decision, does not authorize promotion; the owner must explicitly select an MVP scope. Before implementation, inspect POC artifacts and acceptance evidence and reuse or retire them rather than duplicating native UI, adapters or assembly. Full requirements remain preserved here.
